antidotes.why: Trust that 'I am not the doer' is the antidote named.
Work for the good of all.

chains.summary: Every action has five causes. These are the ground, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and the unseen. Whoever sees the self alone as the doer does not see.
chains.title: Five causes of every result

verses.m: The seat, the doer, the various instruments, the many kinds of effort, and fifth, providence: these are the five causes of every action.
verses.sa: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥

verses.m: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verses.sa: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥

verses.m: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verses.sa: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥

verses.m: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
verses.sa: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥

chains.summary: Bondage is when the mind wants something, grieves over something, rejects, grasps, is pleased or angry. Freedom is when the mind does not. Where there is 'I', there is bondage; where there is no 'I', freedom.
chains.title: What bondage is

verses.m: It is bondage when the mind wants something, grieves over something, drops or grabs something, is pleased or angered by something. It is freedom when the mind does not want, grieve, drop, grab, delight or rage.
verses.sa: तदा बन्धो यदा चित्तं किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति शोचति । किञ्चिन् मुञ्चति गृण्हाति किञ्चिद् दृष्यति कुप्यति ॥ तदा मुक्तिर्यदा चित्तं न वाञ्छति न शोचति । न मुञ्चति न गृण्हाति न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥

verses.m: When there is no 'I', there is freedom; when there is 'I', there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, grab nothing and push nothing away.
verses.sa: यदा नाहं तदा मोक्षो यदाहं बन्धनं तदा । मत्वेति हेलया किञ्चिन्मा गृहाण विमुञ्च मा ॥

depicts.m: When I knew a little, I was blind with pride like an elephant in rut, and my mind swelled: 'I know everything.' When, little by little, I learned from the wise, I realised 'I am a fool', and my pride left me like a fever.
depicts.sa: यदा किञ्चिज्ज्ञोऽहं गज इव मदान्धः समभवम् तदा सर्वज्ञोऽस्मीत्यभवदवलिप्तं मम मनः । यदा किञ्चित्किञ्चिद्बुधजनसकाशादवगतम् तदा मूर्खोऽस्मीति ज्वर इव मदो मे व्यपगतः ॥
depicts.why: Depicts the poet confessing his own I know everything.

depicts.sa: Behind my work was ambition, behind my love was personality,

depicts.m: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice': so they say, deluded by ignorance.
depicts.sa: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया । यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः ॥
depicts.why: Names 'who else is equal to me?'

gloss: The sense that I alone do and own. The Gita: the guṇas act, and the self fooled by ego thinks 'I am the doer' (3.27).

heals.m: Whether the teacher is young, given to pleasures, unlearned, a servant or a householder, do not dwell on it. Who throws away a jewel because it fell in dirt?
heals.sa: बालस्य वा विषयभोगरतस्य वापि मूर्खस्य सेवकजनस्य गृहस्थितस्य । एतद्गुरोः किमपि नैव न चिन्तनीयं रत्नं कथं त्यजति कोऽप्यशुचौ प्रविष्टम् ॥
heals.why: Names pride that refuses wisdom from a lowly source.

heals.m: Alert, deep, steadfast, master of the six waves of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; seeking no honour yet honouring others; capable, friendly, compassionate, wise.
heals.sa: अप्रमत्तो गभीरात्मा धृतिमान् जितषड्गुणः । अमानी मानदः कल्पो मैत्रः कारुणिकः कविः ॥

heals.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
heals.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥

heals.m: Rising by bowing low, making their own virtues known by speaking of others', achieving their own aims by working hard for others, shaming slanderers whose mouths are full of harsh words simply by their patience: the good, whose conduct is a wonder, are honoured in the world. Who would not revere them?
heals.sa: नम्रत्वेनोन्नमन्तः परगुणकथनैः स्वान् गुणान् ख्यापयन्तः स्वार्थान् सम्पादयन्तो विततपृथुतरारम्भयत्नाः परार्थे । क्षान्त्यैवाक्षेपरुक्षाक्षरमुखरमुखान् दुर्जनान् दूषयन्तः सन्तः साश्चर्यचर्या जगति बहुमताः कस्य नाभ्यर्चनीयाः ॥

heals.m: Trees bow low with fruit; clouds hang low with new rain; the good are not puffed up by prosperity. This is the very nature of those who help others.
heals.sa: भवन्ति नम्रास्तरवः फलोद्गमै- र्नवाम्बुभिर्दूरविलम्बिनो घनाः । अनुद्धताः सत्पुरुषाः समृद्धिभिः स्वभाव एवैष परोपकारिणाम् ॥
heals.why: Shows success and humility belonging together.

heals.m: He does not rekindle a quarrel that has died down, does not climb onto his pride, stays calm, and does not do wrong telling himself 'I am in a bad way': the noble call such conduct the best.
heals.sa: न वैरमुद्दिपयति प्रशान्तं / न दर्पमारोहति शान्तिमेति / न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोत्यकार्यं / तमार्यशीलं परमाहुरार्याः

heals.m: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
heals.sa: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते

heals.m: The eight million four hundred thousand kinds of beings, living in water, on land and in the sky: knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Ram, I bow to them with folded hands.
heals.sa: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥
heals.why: The poet begins by bowing to all.

hero.m: From ego come misfortunes; from ego come troubles of the mind; from ego come cravings. There is no enemy greater than ego.

loci.m: From ego come misfortunes; from ego come troubles of the mind; from ego come cravings. There is no enemy greater than ego.

practices.m: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
practices.sa: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
practices.why: Shows humility before a teacher who has seen the truth.

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows devotion as what makes the gift.

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
practices.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥

practices.m: The ear is beautiful through learning, not earrings; the hand through giving, not bracelets; the body of the compassionate shines through helping others, not through sandal paste.
practices.sa: श्रोत्रं श्रुतेनैव न कुण्डलेन दानेन पाणिर्न तु कङ्कणेन । विभाति कायः करुणापराणां परोपकारैर्न तु चन्दनेन ॥
practices.why: Shows the body shining by helping.

practices.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
practices.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
practices.sa: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः

stories.l: Strength without humility is blind. The one blocking your path may be family.
stories.s: Searching for a flower for Draupadi, mighty Bhima finds an old monkey blocking the path and orders it to move. Told to lift its tail himself, he cannot budge it. The monkey is his elder brother Hanuman, who embraces him and teaches him.

stories.l: Wisdom lives in ordinary people doing ordinary work honestly. Care for your parents.
stories.s: A proud ascetic, Kaushika, is sent to learn from a meat-seller in Mithila. The butcher teaches him plain goodness: don't return evil, repent and resolve, keep envy away, care for your parents, and don't spend your one life making enemies.
stories.t: Vyadha Gita: the butcher who taught a sage

stories.l: The moment you boast of beating a weakness, it has found another way in.
stories.s: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.
stories.t: Narada's pride and the monkey face

stories.l: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.
stories.s: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.
